name: Annual register, beneficial-owner and AML pack for associations, juntas vecinales, cooperadoras and similar bodies
buyer: Associations, foundations, juntas vecinales and comisiones vecinales, cooperadoras escolares, sindicatos, comisiones agrícolas, churches and clubs (and juntas de saneamiento) that are legal persons under the Civil Code
trigger: Ley 6446/2019 (art. 9 fines of 50-500 jornales mínimos), Res 8/2022 (Dirección General de Personas y Estructuras Jurídicas y de Beneficiarios Finales): new entities within 45 business days, changes within 15 business days, annual update by 30 June even if nothing changed. Also SEPRELAD Res 490/2022 (OSFL risk-based AML regulation, OSFL are obligated subjects under Ley 3783/09). A 2024 Senate bill on OSFL control and transparency could add accounting duties.
evidence: https://www.ultimahora.com/obligados-registracion-direccion-general-personas-y-estructuras-juridicas-y-beneficiarios-finales-n3034380 (Nov 2022 article: deadlines, penalties, entity types); https://www.abc.com.py/politica/2024/10/05/la-ong-presidida-por-esposa-de-leite-aparece-como-inactiva-ante-seprelad/ (OSFL SEPRELAD status); https://www.diarioconstitucional.cl/2024/10/21/rele-advierte-sobre-proyecto-de-ley-que-limita-la-libertad-de-asociacion-en-paraguay/ (control bill); https://www.abc.com.py/economia/2025/01/16/presupuesto-destinara-a-las-ong-mas-de-g-56000-millones/ (funded NGOs must close accountability returns)
existing: No competitor search run (budget exhausted). The registry itself is a free state portal. The ICNL January 2025 checklist PDF (https://www.icnl.org/wp-content/uploads/Contreras_Enero2025_Informe3-Checklist-w-Logo.pdf) lists the OSFL duties but could not be read (binary fetch).
unchecked: Whether the 30 June annual update is still in force and its exact portal; whether the OSFL transparency bill became law; how many entities are actually registered or in default; whether SEPRELAD OSFL registration requires periodic reports; how to reach thousands of tiny volunteer bodies (federations, municipalities, churches) and their willingness to pay; competitor search in Spanish.

first_check.duty: Ley 6446/2019 with Decreto 3241/2020: register beneficial owners and the legal entity within 45 business days, report changes within 15 business days, and update by 30 June every year. Fines of 50-500 jornales mínimos; ICNL also lists RUC blocking. Ley 7363/2024 (promulgated 15 Nov 2024) with Decreto 4806/2025: existing OSFL must register in SIARA (siara.mef.gov.py, live 1 Dec 2025) within 90 days, and new ones within 30 days. Every year by 30 June they file forms A-E with the DGPEJBF: activities, funding, staff, linked entities and a balance sheet. Every six months they must publish fund-use data on their own website, by the end of July and the end of January. Churches are excluded. Sports clubs, sindicatos, campesino groups, comisiones vecinales and juntas de saneamiento are covered only when they handle public funds for public policy. SEPRELAD registration of OSFL is still required under Ley 1015/97 as amended by Ley 3783/09. Not checked: Ley 7363 sanction amounts, the SIARA deadline actually set, and whether the Episcopal Conference got the extension it asked for. Constitutional challenges were filed (a second one in July 2026). A Senate bill to exempt comisiones vecinales has been postponed.
first_check.market: An ABC Color headline (July 2024) says the law would affect 10,000 comisiones vecinales; I did not open the article. No figures found for registered OSFL in SIARA or for associations in the BO registry (not reached). The likely paying segment is the smaller group of NGOs and foundations that receive public or donor funds, which ABC reports total over G. 56,000 million in the 2025 budget.
first_check.competitor: The only tools found are free state portals: the Abogacía del Tesoro/DGPEJBF registry and MEF SIARA. A Spanish search found no private software or gestoría packaging the annual BO update, forms A-E and the semiannual transparency page; accountants probably do it informally. I found no SaaS for the semiannual transparency publication.
first_check.reason: Both duties are real. Under Ley 6446/2019, associations, sindicatos, juntas vecinales and similar bodies must update the register by 30 June each year, with fines of 50-500 jornales and RUC blocking. Ley 7363/2024 is now in force through Decreto 4806/2025 and the SIARA portal (live Dec 2025). It requires OSFL to file annual forms A-E (including a balance sheet) to the DGPEJBF by 30 June and to publish semiannual transparency data on their own website. Churches are exempt. Comisiones vecinales are covered only if they get public funds, and a Senate bill would ease their rules. The only tools I found are the free state portals; I found no private product. Weak points: legal challenges, volunteer buyers with little money, reaching them.

challenge_check.killer: No killer product found. The scope limits narrow the market. Decreto 4806/2025 (arts. 5-6) excludes churches and covers comisiones vecinales, juntas de saneamiento, sindicatos and similar bodies only if they handle public funds. The core filings go through free state portals (SIARA, the DGPEJBF registry).
challenge_check.reason: Survives, but it is weak. Spanish searches found no private software or packaged gestoría service. The only tools found are free state portals: the DGPEJBF/Abogacía del Tesoro registry and MEF SIARA. Decreto 4806/2025, which regulates Ley 7363, narrows the market. It excludes churches and religious confessions. Comisiones vecinales, juntas de saneamiento, sindicatos, sports bodies and campesino groups are covered only when they receive or administer public funds for public-policy participation. For organisations still in scope, the work is real and recurring: Forms A-E to the DGPEJBF by 30 June, a website transparency publication every six months (end of July and end of January), and SIFEN e-invoicing. The annual beneficial-owner update under Ley 6446 still applies broadly, but it is a simple form on a free portal. Buyers are mostly volunteer bodies with little money. The law is politically contested (constitutional challenges, a June 2026 bill to relax it for comisiones vecinales), which adds repeal risk. No 2026 deadline or extension notice was found.
